title: Thread a plastic divider onto all three rings of a binder and close the rings
instruction: Open the binder's rings, put the loose plastic divider onto all three rings, close the rings with the divider on them, and take your hands off everything.
context: Most adults have filed a sheet into a ring binder: school, work, tax papers. The rings open by a lever and shut again by pushing the half rings together, and a sheet can only go on while they are open. A divider is a wide, stiff sheet whose three holes must meet three rings 108 mm apart at once, and it goes on tilted, hole edge first, along the curve of the open half rings, not straight down. One pinch holds no torque about its closing axis, so a divider held at one point swings about it and its holes miss the rings: it takes a hold at two points along its edge. Order matters: rings opened before the sheet goes on, shut after, and a sheet only hooked on the tips falls off. One hand cannot do both.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +0.305 m and -0.305 m. (1) An Avery Durable View binder with 1 in Slant Rings, item 17011, black (about $9), lies open and flat, spine along y at x 0.400 m, fixed (about 0.45 kg est). Covers 254 x 292 mm, 3 mm thick; spine 42 mm; the rings on the back cover (x above 0.400 m): a steel plate 32 x 254 x 4 mm, three rings on the y axis at y -0.108, 0 and +0.108 m (4.25 in = 107.95 mm pitch, US letter punch), centre line x 0.430 m. Each ring is a half-ellipse 26 mm wide and 27 mm high (about 1 in inside height), wire 4 mm; its far half is fixed, its near half is on a hinge along y at its foot (x 0.417 m, 7 mm over the table); the three near halves and a thumb lever (a 28 x 21 mm bar 33 mm over the table at the plate's -y end, y -0.1455 to -0.1245) are one rigid piece. Rings start shut. Pressing the bar down turns the near halves open (tips 23 mm apart at the 0.80 rad stop); past 0.55 rad (tips 16 mm apart) a detent takes them to the stop; pushing the near halves back under 0.25 rad shuts them, tips together. (2) The loose divider, from an Avery 8-tab plastic divider set (about $6), US letter 279.4 x 215.9 mm (ANSI), orange, 2 mm thick (real about 0.2 mm), 0.05 kg est, three 8 mm square holes (real round about 6.4 mm), centres 12 mm in from the 279 mm punched edge at the ring pitch. It stands in a slanted desk letter sorter on the binder's front cover (build it from 5 mm plastic sheet, about $15: base plate 90 x 300 x 10 mm, a lip 8 mm thick and 26 mm tall 3 mm beyond the divider's lower edge, a backrest 300 x 140 x 5 mm leaning 44 degrees from horizontal on two posts; a clear-plastic slanted letter holder of the same lean also serves): the divider leans 44 degrees against the backrest, punched edge down on the base plate, its far edge 164 mm over the table and its top 76 mm clear of the backrest, at x 0.184 to 0.340 m. Acceptance checks with a tape, protractor and calipers, each within 2 mm or 1 degree: ring pitch, ring height, wire, the lever's travel (bar 33 mm to 10 mm over the table), the open tip gap 23 mm and the sorter's lean 44 degrees. Use a binder from the Durable View line whose rings open by an end lever; if the one in hand does not match, fit a 28 x 21 x 3 mm steel tab to the plate end as the lever.
scoring: Read at the last step from the gate (ring) angle and the divider's pose. Open: the gate 0.55 rad or more open (the tips of the middle ring 16 mm or more apart). Shut: the gate 0.10 rad or less from home (tips 3 mm or less apart). On a ring: for each of the three rings, its wire passes through that ring's hole; with the rings open the wire must pass through the hole at least 8 mm along the wire from its tip, so a hole hooked on a tip alone is not on the ring. Still: the divider moves under 5 mm/s and the gate under 0.1 rad/s. Hands off: every finger zone 30 mm or more from the divider. Score 0 if at any step any part of the divider is more than 3 mm below the table top or past the table's edge. Otherwise: 0 neither open nor on all three rings; 0.3 rings open, divider not on all three; 0.7 divider on all three rings, but not (shut, still, hands off) on every step of the last 1 s; 1.0 divider on all three rings, rings shut, still and hands off on every step of the last 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.3, 0.7, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Real trial: open, a 16 mm spacer block passes between the middle ring's tips; shut, a 3 mm drill bit does not; on a ring, look along each ring: it passes through its hole, and with the rings open the divider cannot be lifted off without first sliding it 8 mm along the wire (mark the wire 8 mm from its tip); still, 30 fps video of the last 1 s, no visible motion; hands off, a 30 mm spacer block against each gripper; fall, by eye against a rule.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Rings: half-ellipses of 4 mm square wire, not D shapes; the mechanism is one rigid hinged piece with a spring and a two-notch detent rule (shut, 0.80 rad open). The thumb lever and tip gaps are design values the real binder must meet (see the setup checks). The divider is a 2 mm rigid plate (real 0.2 mm, flexible), square 8 mm holes, 0.05 kg est. Binder, covers and sorter are fixed.
reset_notes: Stand the divider in the sorter, punched edge down on the lip against the backrest, at x 0.184 to 0.340 m. Rings shut, the lever bar up. The binder open and flat, its spine at x 0.400 m, the sorter on the front cover at x 0.235 to 0.370 m. Nothing is consumed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0; one arm (left idle): 0.3; one arm (right idle): 0.0
